_about: Single source of truth for every rendering, and the auditable term ledger. ONE rendering per referent for the whole book. status per entry: 'attested' (form used in English scholarship), 'provisional' (romanization mine, not found outside), 'decided' (a project style call). Sections are rendered as glossary headings; keys starting with '_' are ignored. This book is Japanese; the 'pinyin' field holds the romaji reading.

石川五右衛門.note: The semi-legendary thief and shinobi who is the novel's hero; by tradition put to death by boiling in 1594.
石川五右衛門.cast: The hero: thief, shinobi, and outlaw.

秀吉.note: Toyotomi Hideyoshi (1537–1598), Nobunaga's foremost general and, after 1582, the unifier of Japan.
秀吉.cast: Nobunaga's general; the coming master of Japan and Goemon's great antagonist.

信長.note: Oda Nobunaga (1534–1582), the warlord who had brought most of central Japan under his power.
信長.cast: The overlord of the realm as the story opens; patron of the Jesuit mission.

タモ.note: A young beggar-woman, burned and half-crippled, taken under Organtino's protection at the Nanban-ji.
タモ.cast: A young beggar-woman, burned and mute with grief, sheltered at the Nanban-ji.

オルガンチノ.note: Gnecchi-Soldo Organtino (1533–1609), Italian Jesuit, for many years superior of the Kyoto mission.
オルガンチノ.cast: Italian Jesuit padre of the Nanban-ji; the beggar-woman Tamo's protector.

信忠.note: Oda Nobutada (1557–1582), Nobunaga's eldest son and heir; commanded the vanguard against the Takeda.

明智光秀.note: Akechi Mitsuhide (1528?–1582), one of Nobunaga's chief generals; the man who would strike at Honnō-ji.

家康.note: Tokugawa Ieyasu (1543–1616), Nobunaga's ally and, in time, founder of the Tokugawa shogunate.

勝頼.note: Takeda Katsuyori (1546–1582), son and heir of Shingen; the last lord of the Takeda.

信玄.note: Takeda Shingen (1521–1573), the great warlord of Kai, Katsuyori's father.

快川.note: Kaisen Joki (d. 1582), Zen abbot of Erin-ji, burned to death with his monks by Nobunaga's men.

穴山梅雪.note: Takeda kinsman and general who defected to Nobunaga and Ieyasu as the house fell.

木曾義昌.note: Takeda vassal in Shinano whose secret defection to Nobunaga touched off the Takeda's final campaign.

村井貞勝.note: Nobunaga's shoshidai (military governor) of Kyoto; a patron of the Nanban-ji, killed defending Nobutada in 1582.

信孝.note: Oda Nobutaka (1558–1583), Nobunaga's third son, joint commander of the projected Shikoku campaign.

佐々木承禎.note: A defeated commander (of the Rokkaku/Sasaki line) sheltered at Erin-ji, as the novel has it.

フランシスコ・ザビエル.note: St Francis Xavier (1506–1552), who opened the Japan mission at Kagoshima in 1549.

ルイス・フロイス.note: Luis Frois (1532–1597), Portuguese Jesuit and the mission's great chronicler.

ガスパル・クエリョ.note: Portuguese Jesuit, vice-provincial of the Japan mission.

ガスパル・ビレラ.note: Portuguese Jesuit, among the first to work in Kyoto (cited here for a report on the peasants).

高山右近.note: The most famous of the Christian daimyo; chose exile over apostasy, dying in Manila in 1615.

服部半蔵.note: Hattori Masanari (1542–1596), 'Hanzo the Devil', the famed ninja captain in Tokugawa Ieyasu's service.
服部半蔵.cast: Ieyasu's ninja captain, of the Iga Hattori line.

カシイ.note: A young Iga shinobi, Tamo's companion, who died shielding her when Iga was destroyed.

カスミ.note: An Iga ninja master, uncle to both Kashii and Etegi, who taught them the arts; died at the Momochi fort in 1581.

明智光春.note: Mitsuhide's nephew; abandoned Azuchi and died at the fall of Sakamoto Castle.

ワリニヤーニ.note: Alessandro Valignano (1539–1606), Jesuit Visitor to the Indies; organized the seminaries and the Tensho embassy.

清水宗治.note: Commander of Takamatsu Castle, who took his own life as the price of the Mori's peace with Hideyoshi.

多羅尾道可.note: Lay-monk and chief of the Tarao, one of the fifty-three houses of Koga; sheltered and guided Ieyasu on the Tarao crossing.

新兵衛.note: Tarao Doka's second son, a handsome, clever seventeen-year-old at the Azuchi seminary and a Christian; he hid the mission's sacred vessels at Oki-no-shima.

藤林長門守.note: One of the two great jonin (upper ninja) masters of Iga.

百地三太夫.note: The most famous jonin of Iga; the Momochi fort where Tamo was maimed was of this house.

エテギ.note: A hugely fat young ninja of Oyamada, twenty-four, good-natured and hopeless at stealth; taken into Ieyasu's service on the Tarao crossing.
エテギ.cast: A vast, good-hearted young ninja, inseparable from the boy Karasumaru.

烏丸.note: A fat thirteen-year-old, orphan of an Ikko-ikki commander, Etegi's inseparable companion.
烏丸.cast: A fat orphan boy of thirteen, Etegi's shadow.

蒲生賢秀.note: Keeper of Azuchi, who spirited Nobunaga's family to safety at Hino after Honno-ji.

柏木四郎兵衛.note: Karasumaru's father: an ex-Mori samurai turned Ikko-ikki commander at Toyama Castle, beheaded by an unknown ninja.

小一.note: Koichi of Higashi-Yubune, the small man who carried the orphaned Karasumaru on his back through six happy years of childhood.

葉津子.note: The daughter of the Shiroko merchant Kadoya Kyuemon, sent to Ieyasu's bed on the night of his escape.
葉津子.cast: A Shiroko merchant's daughter drawn into Ieyasu's orbit.

角屋久右衛門.note: A merchant of Shiroko on Ise Bay, Hatsuko's father, who sheltered Ieyasu the night before he sailed for Mikawa.

信康.note: Ieyasu's eldest son and heir, forced to commit seppuku in 1579 at the age of twenty-one, with Hanzo as his second.

築山どの.note: Ieyasu's principal wife and Nobuyasu's mother, accused of treasonous dealings with the Takeda and killed in 1579.

五徳.note: Nobunaga's daughter, married to Nobuyasu; her twelve-article accusation set his ruin in motion.

酒井忠次.note: One of Ieyasu's chief retainers; his silence before Nobunaga sealed Nobuyasu's fate.

大久保忠世.note: Tokugawa retainer, lord of Futamata Castle, where Nobuyasu died.

一向宗.note: A militant strand of Jodo Shinshu (True Pure Land) Buddhism whose peasant leagues warred with the warlords.

法華宗.note: Nichiren Buddhism; Honno-ji was one of its temples.

ヤソ教.note: Yaso-kyo, from 'Jesus'; the ordinary period Japanese term for Christianity. Rendered 'the Christian faith' / 'Christianity' throughout.

南蛮寺.note: The Jesuit church in Kyoto (Our Lady of the Assumption), completed c. 1576.

安土.note: Nobunaga's castle town on Lake Biwa, seat of the seminary.

本能寺.note: The Kyoto temple where Nobunaga would die in 1582.

比叡山.note: Seat of the Tendai monastery Enryaku-ji, burned by Nobunaga in 1571.

恵林寺.note: The Takeda's devotional temple in Kai, burned with its monks in 1582.

天目山.note: Where Katsuyori and the last of the Takeda died.

有馬.note: Christian domain in Hizen (Kyushu); site of the first Japanese seminary.

臼杵.note: Town in Bungo; site of the Jesuit noviciate.

府内.note: The capital of Bungo (modern Oita); site of a Jesuit college.

伊賀.note: The mountainous province (modern western Mie) famed as a heartland of the shinobi; its self-governing communities were destroyed by Nobunaga in 1581.

越前.note: Province on the Sea of Japan (modern Fukui); the Asakura domain, destroyed by Nobunaga in 1573.

坂本.note: Akechi Mitsuhide's castle town on Lake Biwa.

でうす.note: The Kirishitan word for God, from Latin/Portuguese Deus.

がらさ.note: Grace (Portuguese graça), a loanword of the mission.

おらしょ.note: The Christians' set prayers (from Latin oratio), memorized and handed down by rote.

バテレン.note: Bateren, from Portuguese padre: a Jesuit priest. Rendered 'padre'.

イルマン.note: Irmao (Portuguese 'brother'): a Jesuit lay brother or catechist, below the padre.

念仏.note: The invocation 'Namu Amida Butsu', central to Pure Land practice.

忍者.note: The covert agents of Iga and Koga; rendered 'ninja' or 'shinobi' as the sentence wants.

忍術.note: The shinobi's craft of stealth, evasion, espionage and sabotage.

五遁の術.note: The ninja's arts of evasion, grouped into five (wood, fire, earth, metal, water) and their inner counterparts.

多羅尾越え.note: Ieyasu's flight across Iga after Nobunaga's death; also called the Iga-goe.
